subproblems.title: Open neighbourhoods of the open unit faces: pairwise disjoint and missing every other closed face
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ. For an index pair p = (ι, b) with ι : Fin k → Fin P and b : Fin P → ℤ let Φ_p : Euclid k → Euclid P, Φ_p(y) := b + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} (Lean: WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) 1), and let Q₁ := {y ∈ Euclid k : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}, Cᵏ := {y : 0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1 for all i}. Assume the separation property (S): for all index pairs p ≠ q whose first components are strictly increasing, all y ∈ Q₁ and all y' ∈ Cᵏ, either 1 ≤ dist(Φ_p y, Φ_q y') or min(y_j, 1 − y_j) ≤ dist(Φ_p y, Φ_q y') for some j. Then there is a family (N_p) of subsets of ℝ^P, indexed by all index pairs, such that for every p with strictly increasing first component: N_p is open; Φ_p(y) ∈ N_p for every y ∈ Q₁; and for every q ≠ p with strictly increasing first component, Φ_q(y) ∉ N_p for every y ∈ Cᵏ and N_p ∩ N_q = ∅.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ), (∀ p q : (Fin k → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ), StrictMono p.1 → StrictMono q.1 → p ≠ q → ∀ y y' : Euclid k, (∀ j, 0 < y j ∧ y j < 1) → (∀ i, 0 ≤ y' i ∧ y' i ≤ 1) → 1 ≤ dist (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (q.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y' j • EuclideanSpace.single (q.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) ∨ ∃ j, min (y j) (1 - y j) ≤ dist (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (q.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y' j • EuclideanSpace.single (q.1 j) (1 : ℝ))) → ∃ N : (Fin k → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ) → Set (Euclid P), ∀ p : (Fin k → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ), StrictMono p.1 → IsOpen (N p) ∧ (∀ y : Euclid k, (∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1) → (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) ∈ N p) ∧ ∀ q : (Fin k → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ), StrictMono q.1 → q ≠ p → (∀ y : Euclid k, (∀ i, 0 ≤ y i ∧ y i ≤ 1) → (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (q.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (q.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) ∉ N p) ∧ Disjoint (N p) (N q)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the supplied proof of cmcdtfr_boundary_variation (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1: the open faces F̆_p get pairwise disjoint neighbourhoods N_p), for an arbitrary dimension k. The threshold δ_p(t) = min(1, min_j min(t_j, 1 − t_j)) of the parent proof is written as finitely many strict inequalities. The separation property (S) is the hypothesis; in the parent it is part (c) of cmcdtfr_face_geometry.

Notation. e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1 ∈ ℝ^P; its l'-th coordinate is 1 if l' = l and 0 otherwise. x_l denotes the l-th coordinate of x ∈ ℝ^P, so (Φ_p y)_l = b_l + Σ_j y_j·[ι(j) = l]. For an index pair p = (ι, b) define π_p : ℝ^P → Euclid k by π_p(x) := (x_{ι(j)} − b_{ι(j)})_j (Lean: WithLp.toLp 2 (fun j => x (ι j) − b (ι j))) and d_p(x) := dist(x, Φ_p(π_p(x))) ≥ 0.

1. Continuity. Φ_p is continuous: it is a constant plus the finite sum of the continuous maps y ↦ y_j·e_{ι(j)}. π_p is continuous, because each coordinate x ↦ x_{ι(j)} − b_{ι(j)} is continuous and a map into Euclid k is continuous when all its coordinates are. Hence x ↦ π_p(x)_j and x ↦ d_p(x) are continuous.
2. Left inverse. If ι is strictly increasing, hence injective, then π_p(Φ_p y) = y for every y ∈ Euclid k. Indeed (Φ_p y)_{ι(i)} = b_{ι(i)} + Σ_j y_j·[ι(j) = ι(i)] = b_{ι(i)} + y_i, since ι(j) = ι(i) only for j = i.
3. Definition. Let N_p be the set of x ∈ ℝ^P satisfying all of: 0 < π_p(x)_j and π_p(x)_j < 1 for every j; 2·d_p(x) < 1; and 2·d_p(x) < min(π_p(x)_j, 1 − π_p(x)_j) for every j. The same formula is used for every index pair. If x ∈ N_p, then π_p(x) ∈ Q₁.
4. N_p is open. N_p is the intersection of the finitely many sets {x : 0 < π_p(x)_j}, {x : π_p(x)_j < 1}, {x : 2d_p(x) < 1} and {x : 2d_p(x) < min(π_p(x)_j, 1 − π_p(x)_j)}, for j ∈ Fin k. Each has the form {x : f(x) < h(x)} with f, h continuous by step 1 (a min of continuous functions is continuous), so each is open (isOpen_lt). A finite intersection of open sets is open (isOpen_iInter_of_finite over the finite type Fin k, and IsOpen.inter).
5. The open face lies in N_p. Let ι be strictly increasing, y ∈ Q₁ and x := Φ_p(y). By step 2, π_p(x) = y ∈ Q₁ and d_p(x) = dist(x, Φ_p(y)) = dist(x, x) = 0. So 2d_p(x) = 0 < 1, and 2d_p(x) = 0 < min(y_j, 1 − y_j) for every j because 0 < y_j < 1. Hence x ∈ N_p.
6. Key inequality. Let p and q have strictly increasing first components, p ≠ q, let x ∈ N_p, t := π_p(x), and y' ∈ Cᵏ. Then 2d_p(x) < dist(Φ_p(t), Φ_q(y')). Indeed t ∈ Q₁ by step 3, so (S) applies to p, q, t, y'. If 1 ≤ dist(Φ_p t, Φ_q y'), use 2d_p(x) < 1. If min(t_j, 1 − t_j) ≤ dist(Φ_p t, Φ_q y') for some j, use 2d_p(x) < min(t_j, 1 − t_j).
7. Other closed faces avoid N_p. Let p, q be as in step 6, y ∈ Cᵏ, and suppose x := Φ_q(y) ∈ N_p. With t := π_p(x), step 6 (y' := y) gives 2d_p(x) < dist(Φ_p(t), x) = dist(x, Φ_p(π_p x)) = d_p(x). This is impossible since d_p(x) ≥ 0. Hence Φ_q(y) ∉ N_p.
8. Disjointness. Let p, q be as in step 6 and suppose x ∈ N_p ∩ N_q. Put t := π_p(x) ∈ Q₁, t' := π_q(x) ∈ Q₁, y₁ := Φ_p(t), y₂ := Φ_q(t'), d₁ := d_p(x) = dist(x, y₁), d₂ := d_q(x) = dist(x, y₂) and D := dist(y₁, y₂). Since t' ∈ Q₁ ⊆ Cᵏ, step 6 for (p, q, x, y' := t') gives 2d₁ < D. Since t ∈ Q₁ ⊆ Cᵏ and q ≠ p, step 6 with p and q exchanged (x ∈ N_q, y' := t) gives 2d₂ < dist(y₂, y₁) = D. By the triangle inequality, D ≤ dist(y₁, x) + dist(x, y₂) = d₁ + d₂ < D/2 + D/2 = D, a contradiction. So N_p ∩ N_q = ∅, i.e. Disjoint (N p) (N q).
9. Steps 4, 5, 7 and 8 give all required properties, for every p with strictly increasing first component and every such q ≠ p. For k = 0 the conditions indexed by j are vacuous and Q₁ = Cᵏ is the one-point space; the proof is unchanged, since only the alternative 1 ≤ dist of (S) can occur. ∎
proof_key_steps: π_p(x) := (x_{ι(j)} − b_{ι(j)})_j is continuous and, for strictly increasing ι, a left inverse of Φ_p.

N_p := {x : π_p(x) ∈ Q₁, 2·dist(x, Φ_p(π_p x)) < 1 and < min(π_p(x)_j, 1 − π_p(x)_j) for all j} is a finite intersection of strict inequalities between continuous functions, hence open, and contains Φ_p(Q₁).
(S) gives 2·dist(x, Φ_p(π_p x)) < dist(Φ_p(π_p x), Φ_q y') for x ∈ N_p, q ≠ p and y' ∈ [0,1]^k.
Taking Φ_q y' = x shows Φ_q([0,1]^k) ∩ N_p = ∅. Applying the inequality for (p, q) and (q, p) together with the triangle inequality shows N_p ∩ N_q = ∅.

subproblems.title: The support of ∂Q₀ lies in the union of the closed faces of the representation
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1. Let s be a finite set of index pairs p = (ι, b) with ι : Fin n → Fin P and b : Fin P → ℤ, and let u_p : Euclid n → ℝ be arbitrary functions. Let Q₀ be an n-current on ℝ^P (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) with Q₀(ω) = Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} u_p(y)·ω(Φ_p y)(e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(m)}) dy for every test n-form ω. Here Q₁ = (0,1)ⁿ, Φ_p(y) = b + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} and e_l = EuclideanSpace.single l 1. Then every x ∈ spt ∂Q₀ is of the form x = Φ_q(y) for some q ∈ s and some y in the closed cube [0,1]ⁿ.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the supplied proof of cmcdtfr_boundary_variation, which proves spt Q₀ ⊆ ⋃_q F_q and spt ∂Q₀ ⊆ spt Q₀. Here the two inclusions are merged into one vanishing argument for ∂Q₀.

Notation. e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1, E_q := (e_{ι_q(0)}, …, e_{ι_q(m)}), Cⁿ := {y ∈ Euclid n : 0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1 ∀ i} and Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 ∀ i} ⊆ Cⁿ. Recall the SimonGMT definitions. ∂Q₀(γ) = Q₀(dγ), where dγ = exteriorDerivative γ (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply, exteriorDerivativeTestOn). A current S on univ vanishes on W if S(γ) = 0 for every test form γ with tsupport γ ⊆ W. zeroRegion S is the union of the open sets W with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ univ and S vanishing on W. Finally, spt S := univ ∖ zeroRegion S.

1. Z := ⋃_{q∈s} Φ_q(Cⁿ) is compact, hence closed. Cⁿ is closed: it is an intersection of the closed sets {y_i ≥ 0} and {y_i ≤ 1}, since coordinates are continuous. It is bounded, since each coordinate lies in [0, 1] and so ‖y‖ ≤ √n. Hence Cⁿ is compact in the finite-dimensional space Euclid n (Metric.isCompact_of_isClosed_isBounded). Each Φ_q is continuous (a constant plus the finite sum of y ↦ y_j e_{ι_q(j)}), so Φ_q(Cⁿ) is compact (IsCompact.image). A finite union of compact sets is compact (Finset.isCompact_biUnion), and compact subsets of a metric space are closed (IsCompact.isClosed).
2. A good ball. Fix x ∉ Z. Since Zᶜ is open, there is r > 0 with W := ball(x, r) ⊆ Zᶜ (Metric.isOpen_iff). W is open. closure W ⊆ closedBall(x, r), which is compact in the proper space ℝ^P (isCompact_closedBall). So closure W is compact, as a closed subset of a compact set, and closure W ⊆ univ.
3. ∂Q₀ vanishes on W. Let γ ∈ TestFormOn univ m with tsupport γ ⊆ W. Then ∂Q₀(γ) = Q₀(dγ), and tsupport(dγ) ⊆ tsupport γ ⊆ W (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset). The representation hypothesis, applied to the test (m+1)-form dγ, gives ∂Q₀(γ) = Σ_{q∈s} ∫_{Q₁} u_q(y)·dγ(Φ_q y)(E_q) dy. For q ∈ s and y ∈ Q₁ ⊆ Cⁿ we have Φ_q(y) ∈ Z, so Φ_q(y) ∉ W ⊇ tsupport(dγ). Hence dγ(Φ_q y) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport), and the integrand u_q(y)·0 vanishes at every y ∈ Q₁. So every integral is 0 (setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero), and ∂Q₀(γ) = 0.
4. By steps 2 and 3, W is one of the sets whose union is zeroRegion(∂Q₀). As x ∈ W, x ∈ zeroRegion(∂Q₀), so x ∉ spt ∂Q₀.
5. By contraposition of steps 2–4, every x ∈ spt ∂Q₀ lies in Z. So x = Φ_q(y) for some q ∈ s and y ∈ Cⁿ. ∎
proof_key_steps: Z := ⋃_{q∈s} Φ_q([0,1]ⁿ) is compact, hence closed.
For x ∉ Z some ball W = B(x, r) misses Z; W is open with compact closure.
If tsupport γ ⊆ W then ∂Q₀(γ) = Q₀(dγ) = Σ_q ∫_{Q₁} u_q(y)·dγ(Φ_q y)(E_q) dy = 0, because tsupport dγ ⊆ tsupport γ ⊆ W misses every Φ_q(Q₁).
So x lies in the zero region of ∂Q₀. Hence spt ∂Q₀ ⊆ Z.

subproblems.title: Coordinate covector dx^I exists as a continuous determinant covector (accepted theorem, reused)
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ and every map I : Fin n → Fin P (no monotonicity or injectivity assumed), there is an n-covector θ on ℝ^P with θ(v) = det(Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k)) for every v : Fin n → ℝ^P. Here an n-covector is an element of Covector (Euclid P) n, a continuous alternating n-linear map ℝ^P → ℝ, and Euclid P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P). In words, θ(v) is the determinant of the n×n matrix whose (k, j) entry is the I(k)-th coordinate of v_j.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (I : Fin n → Fin P), ∃ θ : Covector (Euclid P) n, ∀ v : Fin n → Euclid P, θ v = Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k))
subproblems.natural_proof:
This is the comparator-accepted theorem of DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.mass_representation-a1.coordinate_covectors-a1.det_covector_exists-a1. It is reused with its identical frozen type, and its accepted proof is reproduced here.
Source: supplied proof of cmr_coordinate_covectors_span, step 1 (Part (a)), for a single I, with the continuity estimate written out.

Notation:
- ℝ^P := Euclid P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P).
- For x ∈ ℝ^P and l ∈ Fin P, x(l) (Lean: x l) is the l-th coordinate of x.
- An n-covector is an element of Covector (Euclid P) n = (Euclid P) [⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ.

1. (Coordinate projection.) Fix P, n and I : Fin n → Fin P. Define p_I : ℝ^P → (Fin n → ℝ) by p_I(x) := (fun k => x(I k)). Since (x + y)(l) = x(l) + y(l) and (c•x)(l) = c·x(l), p_I is ℝ-linear. Regard it as p_I : ℝ^P →ₗ[ℝ] (Fin n → ℝ).

2. (Determinant as an alternating map.) Θ := Matrix.detRowAlternating : (Fin n → ℝ) [⋀^Fin n]→ₗ[ℝ] ℝ is alternating and multilinear. Θ(u) = det(Matrix.of u) is the determinant of the matrix whose j-th row is u j. Put θ⁰ := Θ.compLinearMap p_I : ℝ^P [⋀^Fin n]→ₗ[ℝ] ℝ. By AlternatingMap.compLinearMap_apply, for every v : Fin n → ℝ^P,
   θ⁰(v) = Θ(fun j => p_I(v j)) = det(Matrix.of fun j k => v j (I k)).

3. (Transpose.) The transpose of Matrix.of fun j k => v j (I k) is Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k). Since det Mᵀ = det M (Matrix.det_transpose), θ⁰(v) = det(Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k)) for every v.

4. (Multiplicative bound.) Fix v and let M := Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k).
   - By the Leibniz formula (Matrix.det_apply), det M = Σ_{σ ∈ Perm(Fin n)} sign(σ)·Π_j M(σ j, j) = Σ_σ sign(σ)·Π_j v_j(I(σ j)).
   - By the triangle inequality for finite sums (Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs) and |a·b| = |a|·|b|, |det M| ≤ Σ_σ |sign σ|·Π_j |v_j(I(σ j))|.
   - |sign σ| = 1, because sign σ = ±1 (Int.units_eq_one_or).
   - For each j, |v_j(I(σ j))| ≤ ‖v_j‖, because a coordinate of a vector of ℝ^P is bounded by its Euclidean norm (PiLp.norm_apply_le).
   - All factors are nonnegative, so Π_j |v_j(I(σ j))| ≤ Π_j ‖v_j‖ (Finset.prod_le_prod₀).
   - There are card(Perm(Fin n)) = n! permutations (Fintype.card_perm, Fintype.card_fin). Summing over them gives
     ‖θ⁰(v)‖ = |det M| ≤ n!·Π_j ‖v_j‖.

5. (Continuity and conclusion.) By step 4, AlternatingMap.mkContinuous applies to θ⁰ with constant n!. So θ := θ⁰.mkContinuous (n!) (bound of step 4) ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n is a continuous alternating map whose underlying function is definitionally that of θ⁰. By step 3, θ(v) = θ⁰(v) = det(Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k)) for every v : Fin n → ℝ^P. This θ witnesses the claim.

6. (Degenerate cases.) No property of I was used. For n = 0 nothing changes: Perm(Fin 0) has exactly one element and the empty product is 1. The bound then reads |det| ≤ 1, and θ is the constant map 1, the determinant of the empty matrix.
proof_key_steps: p_I x := (x(I k))_k is linear; θ⁰ := Matrix.detRowAlternating.compLinearMap p_I is alternating n-linear.
Matrix.det_transpose rewrites θ⁰ v as det(Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k)).
The Leibniz formula, |x(l)| ≤ ‖x‖ and card Perm(Fin n) = n! give |θ⁰ v| ≤ n!·Π_j ‖v_j‖.
θ := θ⁰.mkContinuous n! is an n-covector with θ v = det(Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k)).

subproblems.title: Kronecker property dx^I(e_J) = δ_IJ for strictly increasing I, J (accepted theorem, reused)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let I, J : Fin n → Fin P be strictly increasing, and let θ be an n-covector on ℝ^P (θ ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n) with θ(v) = det(Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k)) for every v : Fin n → ℝ^P. Let e_i := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i be the standard basis vectors of ℝ^P. Then θ(fun j => e_{J j}) = 1 if I = J, and θ(fun j => e_{J j}) = 0 if I ≠ J.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (I J : Fin n → Fin P) (θ : Covector (Euclid P) n), StrictMono I → StrictMono J → (∀ v : Fin n → Euclid P, θ v = Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k))) → θ (fun j => EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ (J j)) = if I = J then 1 else 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
This is the comparator-accepted theorem of DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.mass_representation-a1.coordinate_covectors-a1.det_covector_kronecker-a1. It is reused with its identical frozen type, and its accepted proof is reproduced here.
Source: supplied proof of cmr_coordinate_covectors_span, step 2 (Kronecker property), with θ_I replaced by an arbitrary covector satisfying the determinant identity.

Notation:
- e_i := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i for i ∈ Fin P.
- e_J := (fun j => e_{J j}) : Fin n → ℝ^P.
- For x ∈ ℝ^P, x(l) is its l-th coordinate.

1. (Reduction to a determinant.) Applying the hypothesis on θ to v := e_J gives θ(e_J) = det M with M := Matrix.of fun k j => e_{J j}(I k).

2. (Entries of M.) e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply). The l-th coordinate of EuclideanSpace.single i 1 is 1 if l = i and 0 otherwise (PiLp.single_apply, formerly EuclideanSpace.single_apply). Hence M k j = (if I k = J j then 1 else 0) for all k, j ∈ Fin n.

3. (Case I = J.) Then M k j = (if J k = J j then 1 else 0). J is strictly increasing, hence injective (StrictMono.injective), so J k = J j ↔ k = j. Thus M k j = (if k = j then 1 else 0) = (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) k j (Matrix.one_apply). So M = 1 and θ(e_J) = det 1 = 1 (Matrix.det_one), which is the value of (if I = J then 1 else 0) in this case.

4. (Case I ≠ J: an index of I missing from J.) We show that some k₀ ∈ Fin n has I k₀ ∉ range J. Suppose not.
   - Then I k ∈ range J for every k, i.e. range I ⊆ range J.
   - I and J are strictly increasing, hence injective. So range I and range J are finite sets with exactly card(Fin n) = n elements each (Set.ncard_range_of_injective, Nat.card_eq_fintype_card, Fintype.card_fin).
   - A subset of a finite set with at least as many elements equals that set (Set.eq_of_subset_of_ncard_le), so range I = range J.
   - Two strictly increasing maps on the well-ordered type Fin n with the same range are equal (StrictMono.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT). Hence I = J, contradicting I ≠ J.

5. (Case I ≠ J: a zero row.) Take k₀ from step 4. For every j ∈ Fin n, I k₀ ≠ J j, since I k₀ = J j would put I k₀ in range J. By step 2, M k₀ j = 0 for all j. So the k₀-th row of M is zero and det M = 0 (Matrix.det_eq_zero_of_row_eq_zero). Hence θ(e_J) = 0, which is the value of (if I = J then 1 else 0) in this case.

6. (Conclusion.) By steps 3 and 5, θ(fun j => e_{J j}) = (if I = J then 1 else 0). Degenerate dimensions need no separate treatment:
   - For n = 0, the only map Fin 0 → Fin P gives I = J, and step 3 applies; the empty matrix is the identity, with determinant 1.
   - For n > P, no strictly increasing I exists, so the statement holds vacuously.
proof_key_steps: θ(e_J) = det M with M k j = if I k = J j then 1 else 0, by basisFun_apply and the coordinates of single.
If I = J, injectivity of J gives M = 1, so θ(e_J) = det 1 = 1.
If I ≠ J, range I ⊆ range J would force range I = range J (both have n elements) and then I = J by StrictMono.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT; so some I k₀ ∉ range J.
Row k₀ of M is zero, so θ(e_J) = det M = 0 (Matrix.det_eq_zero_of_row_eq_zero).

subproblems.title: Coordinate m-covectors dual to the codimension-one faces of a coordinate (m+1)-plane
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let ι : Fin (m+1) → Fin P be strictly increasing, and write e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1 ∈ ℝ^P. There are m-covectors ε_0, …, ε_m on ℝ^P (ε : Fin (m+1) → Covector (Euclid P) m) with the following two properties for every c : Fin (m+1) → ℝ. (a) covectorEuclideanNorm(Σ_j c_j ε_j) = √(Σ_j c_j²), using the Euclidean coefficient norm of Simon 6.1.15. (b) For every j ∈ Fin (m+1), (Σ_{j'} c_{j'} ε_{j'})(fun k => e_{ι(j.succAbove k)}) = (−1)^j c_j. In words: evaluated on the tuple (e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(m)}) with its j-th vector removed, the form gives (−1)^j c_j.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (ι : Fin (m + 1) → Fin P), StrictMono ι → ∃ ε : Fin (m + 1) → Covector (Euclid P) m, (∀ c : Fin (m + 1) → ℝ, covectorEuclideanNorm (∑ j, c j • ε j) = Real.sqrt (∑ j, c j ^ 2)) ∧ ∀ (c : Fin (m + 1) → ℝ) (j : Fin (m + 1)), (∑ j', c j' • ε j') (fun k => EuclideanSpace.single (ι (j.succAbove k)) (1 : ℝ)) = (-1) ^ (j : ℕ) * c j
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the supplied proof of cmcdtfr_boundary_variation, which sets ε_j := (−1)^j dx^{ι∘succAbove j}. The determinant covectors dx^J and their Kronecker property come from the sibling theorems det_covector_exists (cmr_cc_det_covector_exists) and det_covector_kronecker (cmr_cc_det_covector_basis_kronecker).

Notation. e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1 = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ l (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply). For J : Fin m → Fin P put e_J := (fun k => e_{J k}). For j ∈ Fin (m+1) put J_j := ι ∘ j.succAbove : Fin m → Fin P. By definition, covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I : Fin m → Fin P} [I strictly increasing]·α(e_I)²), where e_I is written with basisFun.

1. Each J_j is strictly increasing: it is the composition of the strictly increasing maps j.succAbove (Fin.strictMono_succAbove) and ι.
2. The map j ↦ J_j is injective. Let j ≠ j'. By Fin.exists_succAbove_eq there is z with j'.succAbove z = j, so J_{j'}(z) = ι(j). On the other hand ι(j) ≠ J_j(k) for every k: J_j(k) = ι(j) would give j.succAbove k = j by injectivity of ι, contradicting Fin.succAbove_ne. Hence J_j ≠ J_{j'}.
3. Construction. By det_covector_exists (with n := m and I := J_j), choose for each j an m-covector θ_j with θ_j(v) = det(Matrix.of fun k l => v l (J_j k)) for all v : Fin m → ℝ^P. Put ε_j := (−1)^j θ_j.
4. Kronecker values. Let I : Fin m → Fin P be strictly increasing and j ∈ Fin (m+1). Apply det_covector_kronecker with its I := J_j (strictly increasing by step 1), its J := I and θ := θ_j (with the identity of step 3). It gives θ_j(e_I) = 1 if J_j = I, and θ_j(e_I) = 0 otherwise.
5. Values of α_c := Σ_{j'} c_{j'} ε_{j'}. Evaluation is linear in the covector (ContinuousAlternatingMap.sum_apply, smul_apply). So for every strictly increasing I, α_c(e_I) = Σ_{j'} c_{j'}(−1)^{j'} θ_{j'}(e_I) = Σ_{j'} [J_{j'} = I]·c_{j'}(−1)^{j'}. By step 2, at most one j' satisfies J_{j'} = I. Hence α_c(e_I) = (−1)^j c_j if I = J_j, and α_c(e_I) = 0 if I differs from every J_j.
6. Part (b). The tuple (fun k => e_{ι(j.succAbove k)}) is e_{J_j}, and J_j is strictly increasing by step 1. By step 2, the only j' with J_{j'} = J_j is j' = j. So step 5 with I := J_j gives α_c(e_{J_j}) = (−1)^j c_j.
7. Part (a). For I : Fin m → Fin P put T(I) := [I strictly increasing]·α_c(e_I)². We claim T(I) = Σ_j [J_j = I]·c_j². There are three cases.
- I strictly increasing and I = J_{j₀}: step 5 gives T(I) = ((−1)^{j₀}c_{j₀})² = c_{j₀}². The right side is also c_{j₀}², because only j = j₀ satisfies J_j = I (step 2).
- I strictly increasing and different from every J_j: both sides are 0.
- I not strictly increasing: T(I) = 0, and no J_j equals I (step 1), so the right side is 0.
Summing over I and exchanging the two finite sums gives Σ_I T(I) = Σ_j c_j²·#{I : I = J_j} = Σ_j c_j². Taking square roots, covectorEuclideanNorm(α_c) = √(Σ_j c_j²).
8. The degenerate case m = 0 needs no change. Fin 0 → Fin P has a single element, the empty map, and it is strictly increasing. J_0 is that map, θ_0 is the constant 1 (the determinant of the empty matrix), and step 2 is vacuous. ∎
proof_key_steps: J_j := ι ∘ succAbove j is strictly increasing, and j ↦ J_j is injective because ι(j) ∈ range J_{j'} ∖ range J_j for j ≠ j'.
ε_j := (−1)^j θ_j, where θ_j is the determinant covector of J_j given by det_covector_exists.
By det_covector_kronecker, (Σ_{j'} c_{j'} ε_{j'})(e_I) = (−1)^j c_j if I = J_j and 0 for every other strictly increasing I.
This gives the face evaluation (b). Summing the squares over strictly increasing I gives the norm identity (a).

subproblems.title: Cut-off lift of a compactly supported vector field on a face, with prescribed tangential divergence
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1. Let p = (ι, b) be an index pair with ι : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing and b : Fin P → ℤ. Let Φ_p(y) := b + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} with e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1, and Q₁ := (0,1)ⁿ. Let N ⊆ ℝ^P be open with Φ_p(y) ∈ N for every y ∈ Q₁. Let g : Euclid n → Euclid n be C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)) with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and ‖g(y)‖ ≤ 1 for all y. Then there is a C^∞ map G : ℝ^P → Euclid n with compact support, tsupport G ⊆ N and ‖G(x)‖ ≤ 1 for all x, such that Σ_{a ∈ Fin n} D(G_a)(Φ_p y)(e_{ι(a)}) = trace(Dg(y)) for every y ∈ Q₁. Here G_a(x) := G(x)_a is the a-th coordinate of G.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (p : (Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ)) (N : Set (Euclid P)) (g : Euclid (m + 1) → Euclid (m + 1)), StrictMono p.1 → IsOpen N → (∀ y : Euclid (m + 1), (∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1) → (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) ∈ N) → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) g → HasCompactSupport g → tsupport g ⊆ {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} → (∀ y, ‖g y‖ ≤ 1) → ∃ G : Euclid P → Euclid (m + 1), ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) G ∧ HasCompactSupport G ∧ tsupport G ⊆ N ∧ (∀ x, ‖G x‖ ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ y : Euclid (m + 1), (∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1) → ∑ a, fderiv ℝ (fun x => G x a) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 a) (1 : ℝ)) = LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (m + 1)) (fderiv ℝ g y)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the supplied proof of cmcdtfr_boundary_variation, step 5 (the cut-off χ) and step 6 (the divergence on F̆_p). G := χ·(g∘π) is the vector field whose coordinates are the coefficients of the test form built in step 5.

Notation. e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1 ∈ ℝ^P and ê_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1 ∈ Euclid n, with coordinates (e_l)_{l'} = [l' = l]. Define L : ℝ^P → Euclid n by L(x) := (x_{ι(j)})_j (Lean: WithLp.toLp 2 (fun j => x (ι j))), c₀ := (b_{ι(j)})_j, and π(x) := L(x) − c₀. L is linear, hence continuous linear (finite dimension). So π is C^∞ with Dπ(x) = L for every x. Smooth means ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞), i.e. of order ∞.

1. Facts on π.
- (i) L(e_{ι(a)}) = ê_a for every a: L(e_{ι(a)})_j = (e_{ι(a)})_{ι(j)} = [ι(j) = ι(a)] = [j = a], because ι is injective.
- (ii) π(Φ_p y) = y for every y: (Φ_p y)_{ι(j)} = b_{ι(j)} + Σ_k y_k·[ι(k) = ι(j)] = b_{ι(j)} + y_j.
2. The compact set K := Φ_p(tsupport g). tsupport g is compact (HasCompactSupport g). Φ_p is continuous (a constant plus the finite sum of y ↦ y_j e_{ι(j)}). So K is compact (IsCompact.image). Since tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and Φ_p(Q₁) ⊆ N, K ⊆ N.
3. A margin. By IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open (K compact, N open, K ⊆ N) there is δ > 0 with cthickening(δ, K) ⊆ N. Put r := δ/3 > 0.
4. The cut-off χ.
- thickening(2r, K) is open (isOpen_thickening) and cthickening(r, K) is closed (isClosed_cthickening).
- cthickening(r, K) ⊆ thickening(2r, K) (cthickening_subset_thickening', with 0 < 2r and r < 2r).
- So exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff applies (ℝ^P is finite-dimensional; order ⊤ : ℕ∞). It gives a C^∞ function χ : ℝ^P → ℝ with range χ ⊆ [0, 1], support χ = thickening(2r, K), and χ(x) = 1 for x ∈ cthickening(r, K).
- tsupport χ = closure(thickening(2r, K)) ⊆ cthickening(2r, K) (closure_thickening_subset_cthickening) ⊆ cthickening(δ, K) (cthickening_mono, 2r ≤ δ) ⊆ N.
- cthickening(2r, K) is compact (IsCompact.cthickening; ℝ^P is a proper space).
5. Definition and basic properties. Put G(x) := χ(x)·g(π(x)).
- (a) G is C^∞: g∘π is C^∞ (ContDiff.comp), χ is C^∞, and a scalar product of C^∞ maps is C^∞ (ContDiff.smul).
- (b) Support: if χ(x) = 0 then G(x) = 0. So support G ⊆ support χ and tsupport G ⊆ tsupport χ ⊆ cthickening(2r, K) ⊆ N. In particular tsupport G is a closed subset of a compact set, so G has compact support.
- (c) Bound: ‖G(x)‖ = |χ(x)|·‖g(π x)‖ ≤ 1·1 = 1, since 0 ≤ χ(x) ≤ 1 and ‖g‖ ≤ 1.
6. Local agreement with g∘π. Let y ∈ Q₁ and x₀ := Φ_p(y), so that π(x₀) = y by 1(ii). We show that G and g∘π agree on a neighbourhood of x₀. There are two cases.
- Case A, y ∈ tsupport g. Then x₀ ∈ K ⊆ thickening(r, K) (self_subset_thickening, r > 0). This set is open and lies in cthickening(r, K) (thickening_subset_cthickening), where χ = 1. On it, G = g∘π.
- Case B, y ∉ tsupport g. O := (tsupport g)ᶜ is an open neighbourhood of y on which g = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). As π is continuous with π(x₀) = y, π⁻¹(O) is an open neighbourhood of x₀. On it g∘π = 0 and G = χ·0 = 0.
7. Derivative of each coordinate. Fix a ∈ Fin n. By step 6, x ↦ G(x)_a and x ↦ g(π x)_a agree near x₀, so they have the same derivative at x₀ (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq). Apply the chain rule: g is differentiable at π(x₀) = y, Dπ(x₀) = L, and v ↦ v_a is continuous linear. This gives D(G_a)(x₀)(v) = (Dg(y)(L v))_a for all v. With v := e_{ι(a)} and step 1(i), D(G_a)(Φ_p y)(e_{ι(a)}) = (Dg(y)(ê_a))_a.
8. Trace. For a linear map A : Euclid n → Euclid n, trace A = Σ_a (A ê_a)_a. Indeed, use LinearMap.trace_eq_matrix_trace with the basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun, whose vectors are the ê_a and whose coordinate functionals are v ↦ v_a (basisFun_repr). Then trace A = Σ_a (toMatrix A)_{a,a} = Σ_a (A ê_a)_a (LinearMap.toMatrix_apply). Now sum step 7 over a, with A := Dg(y): Σ_a D(G_a)(Φ_p y)(e_{ι(a)}) = Σ_a (Dg(y) ê_a)_a = trace(Dg(y)).
9. Steps 5 and 8 give all required properties. If g = 0, then K = ∅, χ = 0 and G = 0; Case B always applies and both sides in step 8 are 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: π(x) := (x_{ι(j)} − b_{ι(j)})_j is affine with linear part L, L(e_{ι(a)}) = ê_a and π∘Φ_p = id.
K := Φ_p(tsupport g) is a compact subset of N. A smooth cut-off χ with values in [0,1] equals 1 on cthickening(r, K) and has tsupport χ ⊆ cthickening(2r, K) ⊆ N (smooth Urysohn lemma).
G := χ·(g∘π) is smooth, compactly supported in N, satisfies ‖G‖ ≤ 1, and coincides with g∘π near every Φ_p(y), y ∈ Q₁.
By the chain rule, D(G_a)(Φ_p y)(e_{ι(a)}) = (Dg(y) ê_a)_a. Summing over a gives trace Dg(y).

subproblems.title: Admissible test m-form whose exterior derivative on the face is the divergence of g

Let N ⊆ ℝ^P be open with Φ_p(y) ∈ N for all y ∈ Q₁ = (0,1)ⁿ, where Φ_p(y) = b + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} and e_l = EuclideanSpace.single l 1. Source: steps 5–6 of the supplied proof of cmcdtfr_boundary_variation, which build γ(x) := χ(x) Σ_j g_j(π x) ε_j and compute its exterior derivative. Here γ is assembled from the siblings face_covectors (the covectors ε_j) and cutoff_field (the field G = χ·(g∘π)).

Notation. e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1, E := (fun j => e_{ι(j)}) = (e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(m)}), and x₀ := Φ_p(y). By definition Fin.removeNth i E = (fun k => E(i.succAbove k)) = (fun k => e_{ι(i.succAbove k)}).

1. Apply face_covectors to ι. It gives covectors ε_0, …, ε_m such that, for all c : Fin (m+1) → ℝ and all j: (a) covectorEuclideanNorm(Σ_j c_j ε_j) = √(Σ_j c_j²); (b) (Σ_{j'} c_{j'} ε_{j'})(fun k => e_{ι(j.succAbove k)}) = (−1)^j c_j.
2. Apply cutoff_field to (P, m, p, N, g). It gives a C^∞ map G : ℝ^P → Euclid n with compact support, tsupport G ⊆ N and ‖G(x)‖ ≤ 1, such that Σ_a D(G_a)(Φ_p y)(e_{ι(a)}) = trace(Dg(y)) for y ∈ Q₁, where G_a(x) := G(x)_a.
3. Definition. ω(x) := Σ_j G_j(x)·ε_j ∈ Covector(ℝ^P, m).
4. Smoothness. Each G_j = (v ↦ v_j)∘G is C^∞, as the composition with the continuous linear coordinate functional EuclideanSpace.proj j. Hence x ↦ G_j(x)·ε_j is C^∞ (ContDiff.smul with the constant ε_j), and so is the finite sum ω (ContDiff.sum).
5. Support. If G(x) = 0 then every G_j(x) = 0 and ω(x) = 0. So support ω ⊆ support G and tsupport ω ⊆ tsupport G ⊆ N. ω has compact support (HasCompactSupport.mono'), since tsupport ω is a closed subset of the compact tsupport G. Hence ω is a test form with tsupport ω ⊆ univ: γ := ω ∈ TestFormOn univ m, and tsupport γ ⊆ N.
6. Norm. Fix x. By (a) with c_j := G_j(x), covectorEuclideanNorm(γ(x)) = √(Σ_j G_j(x)²) = ‖G(x)‖ (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq and |t|² = t²) ≤ 1.
7. Exterior derivative. Let y ∈ Q₁.
- γ is C^∞, hence differentiable at x₀. The coordinate formula (SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_apply) gives dγ(x₀)(E) = Σ_i (−1)^i·D[x ↦ γ(x)(Fin.removeNth i E)](x₀)(e_{ι(i)}).
- By (b) with c_j := G_j(x) and j := i, γ(x)(Fin.removeNth i E) = (−1)^i G_i(x) for every x. So the i-th function differentiated is (−1)^i·G_i. Its derivative at x₀ is (−1)^i·D(G_i)(x₀) (fderiv_const_mul; G_i is differentiable).
- So the i-th term is (−1)^i·(−1)^i·D(G_i)(x₀)(e_{ι(i)}) = D(G_i)(x₀)(e_{ι(i)}), since ((−1)^i)² = 1.
- Summing over i and using step 2: dγ(Φ_p y)(E) = Σ_i D(G_i)(Φ_p y)(e_{ι(i)}) = trace(Dg(y)).
8. Steps 5–7 give the three required properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take ε_j from face_covectors (for ι) and G from cutoff_field, and set γ(x) := Σ_j G_j(x)·ε_j.
γ is C^∞ with tsupport γ ⊆ tsupport G ⊆ N compact. By the norm identity, covectorEuclideanNorm(γ(x)) = ‖G(x)‖ ≤ 1.
The face evaluation gives γ(x)(removeNth i E) = (−1)^i G_i(x). Then exteriorDerivative_apply gives dγ(Φ_p y)(E) = Σ_i D(G_i)(Φ_p y)(e_{ι(i)}) = trace Dg(y).

subproblems.title: Local mass is superadditive over finitely many pairwise disjoint regions
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P and S an n-current in U (GeometricCurrentOn U n). Let ι be a type, s a finite subset of ι, and N : ι → Set(ℝ^P) with N_i ∩ N_j = ∅ for all distinct i, j ∈ s. Then Σ_{i∈s} M_{N_i}(S) ≤ M_{⋃_{i∈s} N_i}(S) in [0, ∞]. Here M_W(S) = S.massOn W is the supremum of ofReal(S ω) over test n-forms ω in U with tsupport ω ⊆ W and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ι : Type) (s : Finset ι) (N : ι → Set (Euclid P)), (↑s : Set ι).PairwiseDisjoint N → ∑ i ∈ s, S.massOn (N i) ≤ S.massOn (⋃ i ∈ s, N i)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 9 of the supplied proof of cmcdtfr_boundary_variation, which glues near-optimal forms on the pairwise disjoint N_p. Here it is stated for an arbitrary current and an arbitrary finite disjoint family.

Notation. W := ⋃_{i∈s} N_i. For A ⊆ ℝ^P, Adm(A) := massAdmissibleOn U n A = {ω ∈ TestFormOn U n : tsupport ω ⊆ A and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x}. M_A(S) := S.massOn A = sSup{ofReal(S ω) : ω ∈ Adm(A)}. Write |·| := covectorEuclideanNorm.

1. Gluing. Let ω_i ∈ Adm(N_i) for i ∈ s, and let ω := Σ_{i∈s} ω_i, a sum in the submodule TestFormOn U n. So ω ∈ TestFormOn U n and ω(x) = Σ_{i∈s} ω_i(x) (Submodule.coe_sum, Finset.sum_apply). We claim ω ∈ Adm(W) and S(ω) = Σ_{i∈s} S(ω_i).
- (a) S is linear, so S(ω) = Σ_{i∈s} S(ω_i) (map_sum).
- (b) support ω ⊆ ⋃_{i∈s} support ω_i (Finset.support_sum) ⊆ ⋃_{i∈s} tsupport ω_i. The last set is closed (a finite union of closed sets) and contained in W. Hence tsupport ω = closure(support ω) ⊆ ⋃_{i∈s} tsupport ω_i ⊆ W (closure_minimal).
- (c) Fix x. If ω_i(x) = 0 for every i ∈ s, then ω(x) = 0 and |ω(x)| = 0 ≤ 1 (covectorEuclideanNorm_zero). Otherwise choose i₀ ∈ s with ω_{i₀}(x) ≠ 0. Then x ∈ support ω_{i₀} ⊆ tsupport ω_{i₀} ⊆ N_{i₀}. For i ∈ s with i ≠ i₀, N_i ∩ N_{i₀} = ∅ gives x ∉ N_i ⊇ tsupport ω_i, so ω_i(x) = 0. Hence ω(x) = ω_{i₀}(x) (Finset.sum_eq_single) and |ω(x)| ≤ 1.
2. Monotonicity. For i ∈ s, N_i ⊆ W, so M_{N_i}(S) ≤ M_W(S) (massOn_mono).
3. Reduction. If M_W(S) = ∞, the claim is trivial. Assume M_W(S) < ∞ from now on. By step 2 each M_{N_i}(S), i ∈ s, is finite. Put V_i := M_{N_i}(S).toReal ≥ 0, so that ofReal(V_i) = M_{N_i}(S) (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal).
4. Near-optimal forms. Let η > 0. For each i ∈ s choose ω_i ∈ Adm(N_i) with S(ω_i) ≥ V_i − η, as follows.
- If V_i ≤ η, take ω_i := 0. It lies in Adm(N_i), since tsupport 0 = ∅ and |0| = 0, and S(0) = 0 ≥ V_i − η.
- If V_i > η, then ofReal(V_i − η) < ofReal(V_i) = M_{N_i}(S). By lt_sSup_iff some ω_i ∈ Adm(N_i) satisfies ofReal(V_i − η) < ofReal(S(ω_i)). Since ofReal is monotone, this forces V_i − η < S(ω_i).
5. Glue. By step 1, ω := Σ_{i∈s} ω_i ∈ Adm(W). So ofReal(S ω) ≤ M_W(S) (le_massOn), and therefore S(ω) ≤ M_W(S).toReal (ENNReal.ofReal_le_iff_le_toReal, M_W(S) ≠ ∞). With step 4: Σ_{i∈s} V_i − |s|·η = Σ_{i∈s}(V_i − η) ≤ Σ_{i∈s} S(ω_i) = S(ω) ≤ M_W(S).toReal.
6. Limit. For s = ∅ the sum is 0. Otherwise apply step 5 with η := ε/|s| for each ε > 0, getting Σ_{i∈s} V_i ≤ M_W(S).toReal + ε. By le_of_forall_pos_le_add, Σ_{i∈s} V_i ≤ M_W(S).toReal.
7. Conclusion. Σ_{i∈s} M_{N_i}(S) = Σ_{i∈s} ofReal(V_i) = ofReal(Σ_{i∈s} V_i) (ENNReal.ofReal_sum_of_nonneg, V_i ≥ 0) ≤ ofReal(M_W(S).toReal) = M_W(S), by monotonicity of ofReal and ENNReal.ofReal_toReal. ∎
proof_key_steps: Forms ω_i admissible for the pairwise disjoint N_i have at most one nonzero value at each point. So Σ ω_i is admissible for ⋃ N_i, and S(Σ ω_i) = Σ S(ω_i).
If M_{⋃N}(S) = ∞ there is nothing to prove. Otherwise every M_{N_i}(S) is finite.
Choose ω_i with S(ω_i) ≥ M_{N_i}(S).toReal − η and glue them: Σ_i M_{N_i}(S).toReal − |s|η ≤ M_{⋃N}(S).toReal.
Let η → 0 and convert back to [0, ∞] with ofReal.
